title_en: All Mine - The Little Crow with Flowered Socks
source_file: 全都是我的- 花袜子小乌鸦成长故事(3-6 岁).ppt
full_text_zh:
[P1] 花袜子小乌鸦成长故事
全都是我的！
花袜子的夺宝秘诀
（德）示示·吴斯特 文
（德）安妮特·卢道夫 图
王星 译
中国少年儿童出版社
中国少年儿童出版社

[P3] 花袜子小乌鸦总爱拿朋友们的东西。如果有谁一不留神，没把自己的宝贝严严地捂住，牢牢地抓住，紧紧地捆住，秘密地锁住……宝贝就会落到花袜子手里。不知从什么时候起，大家的好东西全都跑到乌鸦窝里去了。花袜子有个坏习惯，一看见好东西就想占为己有。一天，刺猬刚把玩具泰迪熊放在洞口，转身功夫，花袜子飞了过去，玩具熊不翼而飞。这一招叫顺手牵羊！从那以后，大家全都知道要提防花袜子。于是，花袜子想出了五花八门的招术。

[P4] “休想骗走我新买的溜冰鞋。”花袜子一飞过来，猪宝马上提高了警惕。花袜子却跟他聊起了吃的：布丁、巧克力、干果、冰激凌……馋得猪宝直流口水。
“哎，”花袜子逗他，“那边山坡上还有熟透的橡树果呢！”猪宝终于忍不住了，抬脚就想往山上跑。可穿着溜冰鞋怎么爬山呀？
后来溜冰鞋到哪儿去了？当然跑到花袜子的乌鸦窝里去了！
猫头鹰牢牢抓住自己的金项链，不动声色地看着这一切。
她眨着眼睛想：“这种声东击西的把戏算不了什么。”

[P5] 正想着，花袜子就飞过来了。他落在猫头鹰家门前粗粗的枝丫上说：“哇，你的金项链闪闪发光，太漂亮了！除你之外谁也配不上它。”
猫头鹰听了心里美滋滋的，忍不住摘下项链，慷慨地递给花袜子说：“拿去，你戴上试试。”
花袜子一戴上项链，立刻飞得无影无踪。
“这种花言巧语我一眼就能看穿。”树下的长耳兔暗暗地想。他正躺在柔软的丝绒大枕头上，舒舒服服地享受呢。

[P6] 花袜子早就盯上长耳朵兔了。他用大嘴巴轻轻地碰了碰兔耳朵，呱呱叫着威胁道：“马上滚开，小心我揪掉你的兔耳朵！”
胆小的长耳朵兔撒腿就跑。那只软绵绵的丝绒大枕头，就这样归了花袜子。
狐狸冷眼旁观，觉得这种虚张声势的花招实在太可笑了。他才不屑于这样做呢，丢不起这人！他边想边给自己的玩具闹钟上发条，闹钟欢快地唱了起来。
这时，花袜子又出现了。

[P7] 花袜子趁狐狸进屋的工夫，赶快拧松闹钟上的一个小螺丝，音乐声停了。他对狐狸说：“瞧，不唱了，闹钟坏了。”“你瞎说，哪儿那么容易就坏了！”狐狸不相信。他拧了拧发条，闹钟还是不出声。不管他怎么摇晃，怎么敲打，一点儿用没有。
“什么破玩意儿！”狐狸恼火地说，把闹钟扔到一边。花袜子迅速捡起闹钟飞回家，拧紧螺丝欣赏起音乐来。村后的卷毛羊将这一切看在眼里，心想：“就凭这点儿雕虫小技，不可能把我那顶橘红色的新帽子骗走。”

[P8] 花袜子已经看见那顶新帽子了。他飞到卷毛羊身旁说：“你这顶帽子真好看！特别暖和吧？其实你身上的卷毛那么厚，根本用不着戴帽子。我可冻坏了，只要要点儿东西，让自己暖和起来。”说着，花袜子收起翅膀，缩成一团，打了个哆嗦。
“唉，”卷毛羊心想，“他这么可怜巴巴地求我，就把帽子送给他吧。反正我也不是特别需要。”一顶漂亮的新帽子又归花袜子了。
“低三下四的哀求，在我这儿没用。”旁边的帅狼自信地笑了笑，嘟哝着说。

[P9] 帅狼新买了一辆特别酷的玩具救火车。花袜子故作惊讶地看着救火车说：“哟，你这么大了还喜欢玩具车？”“那又怎么样？”帅狼反问道，“你有意见？”“没，没有。”花袜子小心地往前凑了凑说，“我只是觉得奇怪，你玩儿这种婴儿游戏，就不怕被大家笑话？”帅狼觉得很没面子，对心爱的玩具车一下子失去了兴趣，转身钻回洞里。“谢谢！”花袜子兴高采烈地把玩具车开走了，嘴里还嘀咕道：“冷嘲热讽的激将法也挺管用的。”“这种办法真是小儿科。”松鼠看在眼里，摇头晃脑地说，“我才不在乎被谁笑话呢。”

[P10] 松鼠正在玩儿杂技。他急得直冒汗，因为抛到空中的球总是接不住。
“哦，杂技可没那么容易。”花袜子连哄带骗地说，“我用新消防梯换你的球吧。”
松鼠高兴地跳上梯子，蹦蹦跳跳玩儿了起来。
花袜子马上就后悔了，他又看上了稚仔读的那本大厚书。

[P11] 花袜子摘掉橘红色的帽子，从上面扯下一撮羊毛说：
“嘿，你看，这可是纯羊绒！我很愿意和你一起分享，
你有什么好东西和我分享呢？礼尚往来嘛。”稚仔非常为难。他也想送给花袜子一点儿什么，手中却只有一本书。“好吧，”稚仔说，“这本书我已经读完一半，你拿去分享另一半吧。”话音刚落，书已经不见了。
花袜子打算在乌鸦窝里读一读新到手的书，艾迪熊骑着他的三轮车来了。
“噢，这辆车归我该多好啊！”花袜子心里又痒痒了。

[P12] “唉哟，唉哟，唉哟！”花袜子叫唤起来。艾迪熊停下车，抬头望去。
“唉哟，唉哟，唉哟，我的牙！”花袜子叫个不停。“你是不是牙疼？”艾迪熊瓮声瓮气地问。
“是啊！”花袜子痛苦地叫道，“唉哟，唉哟。疼死了！”“我能帮你什么忙吗？”艾迪熊又问。“不能！”花袜子呲牙咧嘴地说，“谁也帮不了忙，我必须想办法把牙疼忘掉。”“随你吧。”艾迪熊嘴里咕噜着，打算继续骑车去玩儿。就在这时，他忽然觉得花袜子挺可怜的，于是安慰他说：“干点儿有意思的事，也许就能忘掉牙疼。你要骑我的车兜一圈吗？”“好主意！”花袜子马上回答，他想，“装腔作势也挺灵的。”他蹬上三轮车，一溜烟就没影了。

[P13] 现在花袜子只能整天趴在窝里，守着他千方百计搞到手的宝贝。“下来一起玩儿吧！”朋友们喊道。“不，”花袜子说，“我不能下去！”他想了想又补充道，“我得看好自己的东西，不能让它们被谁偷跑、骗走，或者给弄坏了。”“那我们上去找你玩儿吧！”朋友们又喊。花袜子急忙张开翅膀护住所有东西。“别，别来！”他呱呱叫道，“下次再说吧！”朋友们不再理他。大家玩儿起了牛仔和印第安人游戏。第二天他们玩儿的是宇宙幽灵。第三天他们玩儿了一整夜捉迷藏。

[P14] 花袜子只能在树上玩儿他的玩具。总是自己跟自己玩儿，一点儿意思也没有。他得赶快想个办法，不然大家会忘掉他的。花袜子该怎么做呢？“把玩具分给大家一起玩儿？不好！把辛辛苦苦骗来的东西还给大家？更傻！”
可他转念一想，“没有朋友才是最糟糕的事呢！”
花袜子终于想出一个好主意，他把所有东西都从窝里搬了出来。“嗨，朋友们，”他喊道，“你们想看看我得玩具吗？这些宝贝全都是我……
呃……我捡到的！”
full_text_en:
[P1] The Sock Puppet Crow's Growth Story
It's All Mine!
The Secret to Sock Puppet's Treasure
(De) Sisi Wu斯特 Text
(De) Annette Ludolf Illustrations
Wang Xing Translator
China Children's Publishing House
China Children's Publishing House

[P3] The sock-wearing crow always liked to take things from his friends. If anyone wasn't careful and didn't securely cover, tightly hold, firmly tie, or secretly lock away their treasure... it would end up in the crow's hands. Sometime ago, everyone's nice things started ending up in the crow's nest. The sock-wearing crow had a bad habit: as soon as he saw something nice, he wanted to claim it for himself. One day, the hedgehog just placed the toy teddy bear at the cave entrance, but before turning around, the sock-wearing crow flew over and the toy bear vanished. This trick was called 'stealing while passing by'! After that, everyone knew they had to be careful of the sock-wearing crow. So, the sock-wearing crow came up with all sorts of tricks.

[P4] "No way are you taking my new roller skates," Piggy immediately became alert as Flower Socks flew over. Instead, Flower Socks started talking about food: pudding, chocolate, dried fruit, ice cream... making Piggy drool.
"Hey," Flower Socks teased him, "There are ripe acorns on that hillside!" Piggy finally couldn't resist and started running up the hill. But how could he climb with roller skates on?
Where did the roller skates end up? Of course, in Flower Socks' crow's nest!
The owl tightly held her gold necklace, watching everything without a sound.
She blinked and thought, "This kind of misdirection trick is nothing."

[P5] Just then, Flower Socks flew over. He landed on a thick branch in front of Owl's house and said, "Wow, your golden necklace sparkles so brightly, it's so beautiful! No one else deserves it but you."
Owl felt delighted and couldn't help but take off the necklace, generously handing it to Flower Socks and saying, "Take it, try it on."
As soon as Flower Socks put on the necklace, he flew away without a trace.
"I can see right through this flattery," thought the Long-Eared Rabbit quietly under the tree. He was lying on a soft velvet pillow, enjoying himself comfortably.

[P6] Hua Wa Zi had long been eyeing the long-eared rabbit. He gently touched the rabbit's ear with his big beak and squawked threateningly, "Get away right now, or I'll pull off your rabbit ears!"
Scared, the long-eared rabbit ran off. That soft, fluffy velvet pillow was now Hua Wa Zi's.
The fox watched coldly, thinking this show of bravado was too ridiculous. He had no interest in such tricks—he couldn't afford to lose face! As he thought, he wound up his toy alarm clock, which began to sing cheerfully.
At that moment, Hua Wa Zi appeared again.

[P7] While the fox was entering his house, Flower Socks quickly loosened a small screw on the music box, and the music stopped. He told the fox, "Look, it's not playing anymore—the music box is broken." "You're making it up! How could it break so easily?" the fox said, disbelieving. He wound the key, but the music box still made no sound. No matter how he shook or hit it, it was completely useless.
"What a broken toy!" the fox said angrily, throwing the music box aside. Flower Socks quickly picked it up and flew home, tightened the screw, and enjoyed the music. The curly-haired sheep behind the village watched everything and thought, "With such a petty trick, he can't possibly trick me into giving up my bright orange new hat."

[P8] Hua Wa Zi had already spotted the new hat. He flew over to the curly-haired sheep and said, "This hat looks so nice! Is it really warm? Actually, with your thick curly wool, you don't even need to wear a hat. I'm freezing! I just need something to warm myself up." As he spoke, Hua Wa Zi folded his wings, curled up into a ball, and shivered.
"Oh well," the curly-haired sheep thought, "He's begging so pitifully. I might as well give him the hat. After all, I don't really need it." The beautiful new hat was once again Hua Wa Zi's.
"Pitiful begging won't work on me," the handsome wolf said confidently, smirking and muttering to himself.

[P9] The cool wolf bought a super cool toy fire truck. Flower Socks pretended to be surprised, looking at the fire truck and saying, “Hey, you’re so big now—still liking toy cars?” “So what?” the wolf retorted, “You got a problem?” “No, no,” Flower Socks cautiously leaned in and said, “I just find it strange. Playing with toys like this—don’t you fear being laughed at by everyone?” The wolf felt embarrassed, lost interest in his beloved toy car instantly, and turned back into his cave. “Thank you!” Flower Socks happily drove off with the toy car, muttering to himself, “Mocking and provoking—this method works pretty well.” “Such a trick is really childish,” the squirrel observed, shaking his head, “I don’t care who laughs at me.”

[P10] The squirrel was practicing acrobatics. He was sweating nervously because he always missed catching the ball he threw into the air.
“Oh, acrobatics aren’t easy at all,” said Flower Socks, sweet-talking and tricking him. “I’ll trade my new fire ladder for your ball.”
The squirrel happily climbed the ladder and bounced around, playing.
Flower Socks immediately regretted it. He then spotted the thick book that Little Chick was reading.

[P11] Hua Wa Zi took off his orange hat and pulled a tuft of wool from it, saying:
"Hey, look, this is pure wool! I'd be happy to share it with you.
What nice thing do you have to share with me? It's only fair, after all." Zhi Zai felt very awkward. He also wanted to give Hua Wa Zi something, but he only had one book in his hand. "Alright," Zhi Zai said, "I've already read half of this book. You can take it and share the other half." As soon as he finished speaking, the book was gone.
Hua Wa Zi planned to read his newly acquired book in the crow's nest, when Ai Di Xiong arrived riding his tricycle.
"Oh, how nice it would be if this tricycle belonged to me!" Hua Wa Zi thought, his heart itching again.

[P12] "Aiyoh, aiyoh, aiyoh!" Flower Socks cried out. Eddie Bear stopped his tricycle and looked up.
"Aiyoh, aiyoh, aiyoh, my tooth!" Flower Socks kept crying. "Are you toothache?" Eddie Bear asked in a deep, muffled voice.
"Yes!" Flower Socks cried in pain, "Aiyoh, aiyoh. It hurts so much!" "Can I help you with something?" Eddie Bear asked again. "No!" Flower Socks said, gritting his teeth, "No one can help. I must find a way to forget the toothache." "Suit yourself," Eddie Bear muttered, intending to continue riding his tricycle to play. Just then, he suddenly felt sorry for Flower Socks and comforted him, "Do something fun, and maybe you can forget the toothache. Want to ride my tricycle for a spin?" "Great idea!" Flower Socks answered immediately, thinking, "Putting on an act really works." He hopped onto the tricycle and disappeared in a flash.

[P13] Now, Flower Socks could only lie in his nest all day, guarding the treasures he had worked so hard to get. "Come down and play with us!" the friends called out. "No," Flower Socks said, "I can't go down!" He thought for a moment and added, "I have to keep an eye on my things. I can't let them be stolen, tricked away, or broken." "Then we'll come up to play with you!" the friends called again. Flower Socks quickly spread his wings to protect everything. "No, no!" he squawked, "Next time!" The friends ignored him. They played cowboys and Indians. The next day, they played space ghosts. The third day, they played hide-and-seek all night long.

[P14] Hua Wa Zi could only play with his toys up in the tree. Always playing by himself, it was completely boring. He had to think of a way fast, or everyone would forget about him. What should Hua Wa Zi do? "Share the toys with everyone? No way! Return the things he worked so hard to trick? Even sillier!"
But then he thought, "Having no friends is the worst thing!"
Hua Wa Zi finally came up with a good idea. He brought out all his things from his nest. "Hey, friends," he called out, "Do you want to see my toys? These treasures are all... 
well... I found them!"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《全都是我的！》，副标题为《花袜子的夺宝秘诀》，展示了主角花袜子小乌鸦躺在树下，身边堆满玩具和物品，画面充满童趣。
[P2] 夜幕降临，一轮明月高悬，花袜子小乌鸦躺在树下的巢中，身旁挂着一盏小灯，画面宁静而温馨。
[P3] 本页讲述了花袜子小乌鸦总爱偷拿朋友们的东西，因其‘顺手牵羊’的伎俩而被大家提防，于是他开始想出各种招数。画面描绘了夜晚森林的宁静场景，花袜子在树下休息，周围散落着各种物品。
[P4] 花袜子小乌鸦用美食诱惑猪宝，趁其不备偷走溜冰鞋，而猫头鹰在一旁看穿了他的把戏。
[P5] 花袜子用花言巧语骗取猫头鹰的金项链后迅速飞走，而长耳兔在一旁看穿了他的伎俩，正舒适地躺在枕头上。
[P6] 花袜子用恐吓手段从长耳朵兔那里抢走了丝绒大枕头，狐狸在一旁冷眼旁观并觉得可笑，随后花袜子再次出现。
[P7] 花袜子趁狐狸进屋时，故意弄坏其闹钟并谎称损坏，成功骗走闹钟后飞回家欣赏音乐，而卷毛羊目睹全过程，心想不会被这种小把戏骗走自己的新帽子。
[P8] 花袜子用假装寒冷的手段骗取卷毛羊的新帽子，而帅狼在一旁看穿了他的把戏并嗤之以鼻。
[P9] 花袜子小乌鸦用激将法让帅狼因害羞而放弃新买的玩具救火车，并趁机将其偷走，松鼠在一旁看穿了这一计谋并表示不屑。
[P10] 花袜子小乌鸦用新消防梯骗走了松鼠的球，松鼠高兴地玩了起来，而花袜子随即又盯上了稚仔正在读的大厚书。
[P11] 花袜子用羊毛骗走稚仔的书后，正打算阅读时，艾迪熊骑着三轮车出现，花袜子又心生贪念，想要那辆三轮车。
[P12] 花袜子假装牙疼，艾迪熊同情他并主动让他骑自己的三轮车，花袜子趁机骑车溜走。
[P13] 花袜子因害怕失去偷来的宝贝而拒绝与朋友们一起玩耍，朋友们因此不再理他，转而玩起了各种游戏。
[P14] 花袜子因独自玩玩具感到无聊，担心被朋友遗忘，于是想出一个主意，把偷来的玩具搬出来，假装是自己捡到的，想以此重新获得朋友们的关注。
[P15] 夜晚，一轮明月高悬，花袜子小乌鸦独自躺在巢中，身旁挂着一盏小灯，画面宁静而孤独。
